The older sister’s first share is
\[
40+\frac{40}{x-4},
\]
and her second share is
\[
40+\frac{40}{x+1}.
\]
For both to be whole numbers, \(x-4\) and \(x+1\) must both divide 40. Since their difference is 5, the only possible positive divisor pair is \(5\) and \(10\). Thus
\[
x-4=5 \implies x=9.
\]
So the difference is
\[
\left(40+\frac{40}{10}\right)-\left(40+\frac{40}{5}\right)
=44-48=-4.
\]
\boxed{-4}
